title: TimeSlave Configuration
description: Runtime configuration for the TimeSlave gPTP process. The same schema is used on both Linux and QNX; QNX-specific options live under the optional 'qnx' key.

iface_name.description: Network interface name used for gPTP (e.g. 'emac0' on QNX, 'eth0' on Linux).

pdelay_req_interval_ms.description: Interval between Pdelay_Req transmissions in milliseconds (IEEE 1588 logPdelayReqInterval converted to ms for simplicity).

pdelay_warmup_ms.description: Delay before the first Pdelay_Req after startup in milliseconds.

sync_timeout_ms.description: Declare sync loss after this many milliseconds without receiving a Sync/FollowUp.

jump_future_threshold_ns.description: A time jump greater than this (nanoseconds) is detected as a future jump.

shm_path.description: Shared-memory path used to publish PTP snapshots for TimeDaemon.

phc.description: PHC (PTP Hardware Clock) adjustment settings. If omitted, PHC adjustment is disabled.

device.description: PHC device path. On QNX use the interface name (e.g. 'emac0'); on Linux use the /dev/ptpN path.

step_threshold_ns.description: Offsets larger than this trigger a step correction (nanoseconds); smaller offsets are slewed.

bpf_device_prefix.description: Path prefix for BPF devices used for raw Ethernet frame capture.

see_sent.description: If true, sent frames are also delivered to the RX BPF (used for TX timestamp capture).
